RATIONALE · ARCHITECTURE TRADE-OFFS · FAQS

Why Yav? Architecture & Comparisons

Clear architectural motivations, honest technical trade-offs, and an unvarnished comparison between Yav, client-side WASM, and JavaScript full-stack frameworks.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q1.Why doesn't Yav compile down to WebAssembly (WASM) for the client?

Compiling entire UI component trees to client-side WASM produces massive 2 MB to 10 MB initial bundle sizes, requires complex JavaScript interop bridges for DOM access, and drains battery life on mobile devices during startup. Yav renders pure, clean HTML directly on the server with hyper 1.0 throughput, pairing server power with htmx and declarative CSS/WAAPI for tactile UI.

Q2.How do I handle dynamic client interactivity without React or Vue?

Yav treats htmx attributes (hx-post, hx-target, hx-swap) as first-class citizens in RSX markup. When a user filters a search list or submits a modal form, the server responds with a sub-millisecond HtmlFragment partial that swaps directly into the DOM with zero client-side framework runtime.

Q3.Is Node.js really not required for development or Tailwind CSS?

Absolutely not. The Yav CLI automatically downloads and caches the standalone official Tailwind standalone binary directly from GitHub releases matching your OS architecture. Compilation happens asynchronously on a background thread in milliseconds, without creating a node_modules directory.

Q4.Can I still use JavaScript libraries or Web Components if needed?

Yes. Yav emits clean, standard HTML. You can embed any web component, CDN script (e.g. Mapbox, Chart.js, Monaco), or custom TypeScript script using standard <script> tags or vanilla ESM imports.

Q5.How is Yav deployed to production?

Run cargo build --release to produce a single self-contained native binary, or yav docker to scaffold a multi-stage distroless Alpine container image under 30 MB. It can run on AWS, fly.io, Railway, bare-metal Linux servers, or Kubernetes pods with zero dependencies.

Q6.How does Yav integrate AI, LLM streaming, and Model Context Protocol (MCP)?

Yav provides a first-class native AI SDK in yav::server::ai with streaming Server-Sent Events tokens, Hybrid RAG with cosine vector similarity, and an Anthropic-compliant Model Context Protocol server (yav::server::mcp::McpServer) that exposes your Rust functions directly to LLMs as typed tools.

Q7.Does Yav support enterprise authentication and authorization?

Yes. Yav includes built-in WebAuthn FIDO2 / Passkey authentication in yav::server::passkeys with hardware keys, Touch ID, and Face ID support, coupled with a Google Zanzibar-inspired Relationship-Based Access Control (yav::server::rebac::RebacStore) for sub-millisecond graph authorization checks.

A web framework for people who read the assembly.
